content_html:
Preparing your backpack for Machu Picchu well can make the difference between a smooth experience… or an uncomfortable day.

It's not about carrying more things.
It's about wearing the right thing.

Why is it important to know what to bring to Machu Picchu?

Machu Picchu is a hike in a natural environment.

That means:

  • Constant weather changes
  • Long tours
  • Limited access to on-site stores

If you forget something important, you won't be able to fix it easily.

Checklist: what to bring in your backpack for Machu Picchu

Essentials:

  • Passport or identity document
  • Entrance to Machu Picchu (digital or printed)
  • Cash (soles)

For the weather:

  • Raincoat or rain poncho
  • Cap or hat
  • sunglasses
  • Sunscreen

Hydration and energy:

  • Reusable water bottle
  • Light snacks (nuts, energy bars, fruit)

Comfort during the tour:

  • Small backpack (no larger than 20L)
  • Camera or cell phone with charged battery
  • Power bank (external battery)
  • Wet wipes or toilet paper

Recommended extras:

  • Insect repellent
  • A light change of clothes (optional)
  • Plastic bags (to protect your things from the rain)

Key tip: prepare for rain

Even in the dry season, it can rain.

Therefore:

  • Always carry a raincoat
  • Protect your backpack with a cover or bag

Rain can appear at any time.

What NOT to bring to Machu Picchu

To avoid problems upon entry:

Avoid carrying:

  • Large backpacks (not allowed)
  • Unnecessary heavy objects
  • Drones (restricted)
  • Canes without rubber tips

Common traveler mistake

Many carry too much… or too little.

Result:

  • They get tired faster
  • They forget the essential
  • They don't enjoy the experience

The key is balance: light, but complete.

Travel prepared and enjoy to the fullest

Having the right backpack allows you to:

  • Comfortable walking
  • Enjoy the tour without stress
  • Adapt to the climate
  • Live the experience better
